blindSummary:
This state/province recorded 2 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025 on a population of ~3.3 million, a rate of about 0.61 per million per year, above the national per-million rate. It sits inside the hardest-hit sub-regional concentration the dossiers track: that sub-region absorbed roughly 38 of the 80 national killings in 2025, and this state/province itself recorded 6 in 2024, one of the worst state/provincial counts that year, so its absolute number swung sharply between dossiers. A single additional case would move the rate dramatically at this population.

No unit-specific legal restriction or enforcement finding was identified; the profile rests on the per-capita count, the 2024 toll near the top of the state/provincial table and the regional concentration. A neighbouring state/province of similar size recorded 4 killings in 2025.
blindSourceSummaries: The national trans-association's 9th annual dossier (released 26 Jan 2026, reported by a broadcast news outlet): the country recorded 80 murders of trans and travesti people in 2025, 34% down on 2024 but with at least 75 attempted homicides and crimes marked by excessive violence; in the per-state table the top states/provinces recorded 8, 8, 7 and 7 killings and a middle group 5 each, with this state/province at 2 and one further state/province at 3; 1,261 murders over 2017-2025 (avg 140/year); 97% of victims travestis/trans women, over half aged 18-29, 70% of racially-identified cases were from the country's historically marginalised racial groups; 67.5% of killings happened in interior cities rather than capitals, where monitoring, denunciation and access to public policies are harder; the country has led the global ranking since 2008. Gives this state/province's 2025 count (2) within the per-state ranking.

Association-dossier coverage (27 Jan 2025): the country led global trans-murder tallies for the 16th consecutive year with 122 killings in 2024, a 16% fall on 2023; victim profile predominantly young, poor, from historically marginalised groups and from the country's hardest-hit sub-region, with the population's life expectancy cited at about 35 years; most murders happen in public places, at night, with extreme cruelty; authorities rarely register victims' gender identity, degrading official data; the state-by-state 2024 table places this state/province at 6 killings, among the worst state totals that year, alongside peers at 2, 5 and 8. The association's president demands effective public policies and honest statistics.
